reviewer: Codex distinct question and matching review

questions.text: Selection for jobs or college places should use individual ability and achievement, without preference because of race or sex.
Institutions should help disadvantaged applicants develop the skills needed to compete on equal terms.
Major businesses should be owned and controlled by workers or the public rather than private investors.
The state should be replaced by voluntary associations, including for courts and public safety.
Political power should belong to a single governing party rather than competing parties.

notes: Retained skill-development support, combined hiring and admissions, added three distinct institutional topics.
Each question describes a policy without praise or blame; no preferred score targets.

Social/worker ownership is not identical to state ownership. Stateless voluntary provision does not imply private or collective economic ownership. One-party requirement is scoped to orthodox Marxism–Leninism, not general socialism.
All five items affect defining prerequisites; remaining compatible candidates rank on equal-weight 15-axis distance. No sixth axis or score weighting introduced.
Neutral, missing and opposing answers do not establish prerequisites. Profiles lack new evidence and are excluded from affected templates until assessed, without inventing responses.
This is construct review and regression testing, not empirical psychometric calibration.

Preserved existing historical East Germany reference through separately sourced inferred supplement answers. Revision 3 adds the complete constitution source for Articles 9–12; the GHI excerpt covers Article 1. All 240 country answers remain unchanged.

Supplement evidence revisions 1–3 are generated to public downloads; revision 3 is current. No new personality or country scored assessments were created. The broader policy deliberately fails closed on unassessed prerequisites.
